title: Azure Database Migration Service
description: Learn how Azure Database Migration Service and Data Migration Assistant help you move databases to Azure with minimal downtime.

data.text: Organizations move databases to Azure to reduce infrastructure costs, improve security, gain built-in high availability, and access cloud-native features like automatic scaling and intelligent performance tuning. Migrating a database is more than copying files. It involves schema compatibility, data validation, network configuration, and minimizing downtime for production applications.

data.title: Azure Database Migration Service (DMS)
data.text: Azure Database Migration Service is a fully managed service that streamlines migrations from multiple database sources to Azure data platforms. It supports homogeneous migrations, such as SQL Server to SQL Server, as well as heterogeneous migrations, such as Oracle to Azure SQL Database.

Before you begin a migration, you should assess compatibility and performance. Data Migration Assistant (DMA) is a free standalone tool that scans your source database for issues that could block or slow down a migration. DMA identifies deprecated features, compatibility problems, and performance improvements you can make on the target platform.

data.title: What DMA Checks For
items: SQL Server features that are deprecated or discontinued in the target version.
Breaking changes in T-SQL syntax or behavior.
Missing indexes or statistics that could degrade performance after migration.
Security vulnerabilities and missing permissions on the target.
Schema differences between source and target databases.

data.text: Azure DMS supports several migration paths. The right path depends on your source platform, target platform, and downtime requirements. Some migrations are offline with a cutover window, while others use ongoing replication to keep the source and target in sync until you are ready to switch.

A typical database migration follows a repeatable workflow. Start by assessing the source database with DMA, provision the target Azure service, create a DMS instance, configure the migration project, run the migration, validate the data, and finally update your application connection strings to point to the new database.

data.title: Typical Migration Steps
items: Assess the source database with Data Migration Assistant.
Provision the target Azure database service.
Create an Azure Database Migration Service instance in the same region as the target.
Create a migration project in DMS and select the source and target database engines.
Run a test migration to validate schema and data correctness.
Run the production migration using offline or online mode depending on downtime requirements.
Validate row counts, checksums, and query results.
Update application connection strings and perform a final cutover.

data.title: Create a Database Migration Service Instance with Azure CLI
data.content: Creates a DMS instance in the Standard pricing tier with a system-assigned managed identity.
data.code:
az dms create \
  --name my-dms-instance \
  --resource-group myResourceGroup \
  --location eastus \
  --sku-name Standard_2vCores \
  --subnet-id /subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/resourceGroups/myResourceGroup/providers/Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks/myVnet/subnets/mySubnet \
  --virtual-enterprise-embedding-license-details embed \
  --tags project=migration environment=production

cards.title: Data Migration Assistant (DMA)
cards.description: A free assessment and remediation tool that scans source databases for compatibility issues before migration.

cards.title: Azure Database Migration Service (DMS)
cards.description: A fully managed service that performs the actual data migration from source to target with support for online and offline modes.

cards.title: Export BACPAC
cards.description: A file-based approach that exports schema and data from SQL Server to a BACPAC file for import into Azure SQL Database.

cards.title: Native Tools
cards.description: Database-native tools like pg_dump, mysqldump, and mongodump for source-specific export and import workflows.

data.title: Network Requirements
data.text: Azure DMS requires network access to both the source and target databases. For online migrations, you must configure a virtual network with access to the source. For offline migrations, ensure the DMS instance can reach both databases over TCP 1433 for SQL Server or the appropriate port for your source engine.

terms.definition: The final step in a migration when the application switches from the source database to the target database.
Change Data Capture, a feature that tracks inserts, updates, and deletes on the source database so the target can stay synchronized during an online migration.
A ZIP file that contains a database schema and data, used to move SQL Server databases between environments.
A migration mode where the source database is unavailable to applications during the data transfer and cutover phase.

data.title: Plan a Migration
data.description: You need to migrate an on-premises SQL Server database to Azure SQL Database. The application cannot tolerate more than 15 minutes of downtime.
steps: Identify which Azure Database Migration Service mode you would use: offline or online with CDC.
List the preparation steps you would take with Data Migration Assistant.
Describe how you would validate the migrated data before cutover.
Outline the rollback plan if the target database has issues after cutover.
data.expectedOutcome: You can describe an online migration workflow using Azure DMS and CDC, explain how DMA helps assess compatibility, and outline validation and rollback steps for a production migration.

data.title: Database Migration Service Summary
points: Azure DMS supports migrations from SQL Server, Oracle, MySQL, PostgreSQL, and MongoDB to Azure.
Data Migration Assistant assesses compatibility and identifies issues before migration.
Online migrations use CDC to minimize downtime during cutover.
Offline migrations use maintenance windows for data transfer and validation.
DMS requires network connectivity to both source and target databases.
data.takeaway: Azure Database Migration Service and Data Migration Assistant together provide a structured path from assessment through cutover, making cloud database migrations safer and more predictable.
